title: Lamentations 3:22–23
paragraphs:
“It is of the LORD’S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.
They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.”
— KJV
Brother, this verse was not written in a season of ease.

It was born in ruin.
Ashes.
Grief.
A man staring at devastation and still daring to say, “God’s mercy has not run out.”
That is the shock of Lamentations 3.

You may feel like you wasted too much. Fell too hard. Failed too often. But this text stands up and says, you are still here because mercy kept you. Not your strength. Not your discipline. Not your clean record.

And not recycled mercy.
Not leftovers from yesterday.
New every morning.

That means when you wake up with regret, God meets you with compassion. When shame whispers your story is over, God says His faithfulness is not exhausted. And in Christ, we see that mercy in full color: Jesus took the judgment we deserved so we could receive the grace we never could earn.

Here is the hope:
Your sin may be real.
Your pain may be deep.
But God’s compassion is deeper still.

So breathe again.
Pray again.
Come to Jesus again.

Because the morning did not arrive empty.
It arrived carrying mercy.
